summary: To test ansible-core itself you need a source checkout, not an installed copy. Clone the repo, cd into it, and source hacking/env-setup, or just run bin/ansible-test directly.
questions: How do I run ansible-test against the ansible-core source code?
Is an installed ansible-core enough to test ansible-core changes?
How can I make sure I'm running the source ansible-test and not the installed one?

answer_card.title: Set up ansible-core source for testing
answer_card.answer_md:
An installed ansible-core is neither needed nor sufficient; use a source clone.

```shell
git clone https://github.com/ansible/ansible ~/dev/ansible
cd ~/dev/ansible
source hacking/env-setup   # puts the source programs on PATH
```
If you only need `ansible-test`, skip env-setup and run `bin/ansible-test` from the source root. If you also have ansible-core installed, check `which ansible-test` points at the source copy.
